issues.display_title: Issue #729: fix(wizard): a resumed wizard's Mappedin import drops the user back on Create Project
issues.main_description_html:
Importing a Mappedin export from the wizard can drop the user straight back on Create Project (Step 1, "Select Location" / "Creating project…") with the wizard emptied, the import gone and no error shown. Reported as #727.

The attachment on #727 is not the problem: mall-demo-facility.zip runs through runImport cleanly — 1 building "Mall Demo - Facility", 1 floor "Level 1", 34 locations, 6 categories. The import succeeds and the review modal opens. The user is bounced afterwards, on Continue to Editor.

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

gf_project_id is missing from localStorage by the time the import exit navigates, so bare /editor sends the user to /start.

The chain, on a resumed wizard (a mid-wizard reload, or coming back to /start with a saved draft — what a tester does constantly):

  1. /start mounts useWizardPersistence(undefined, { freshStart: true }) → prepareWizardSession removes gf_project_id (src/lib/persistence/wizardSession.ts:17) while deliberately keeping the blob so the draft can resume.
  2. The blob restore re-attaches the project with store.setWizardProjectId(saved.projectId) (src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts:133) — state only, no localStorage write (src/store/mapStore/projectSlice.ts:58-60, vs setProjectId at :54-57 which does write it).
  3. Step 1's Confirm Location now early-returns: confirmLocationAndProject sees a truthy state.projectId and skips straight to setCurrentSetupStep(1) (src/lib/projects/wizardProject.ts:29-32), so the one writer of gf_project_id on this path never runs.
  4. Step 2 imports the Mappedin zip — fine — and Continue to Editor runs handleContinueToEditor. Its if (!useMapStore.getState().projectId) guard (src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:186) is false, so the setProjectId inside it is skipped too.
  5. completeWizard deletes the wizard blob (src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts:52) — the draft's only client-side copy.
  6. router.push("/editor") (src/components/setup/StepUploadFloor.tsx:204) → src/app/editor/page.tsx:13 reads a null gf_project_id → router.replace("/start").
  7. /start is wizard Step 1 = the Create Project screen. Blob gone, import gone, no message. Repeat the import, land back there again.

The sibling exit already knows about this. src/components/setup/StepGenerate.tsx:108-109 navigates with router.push(projectId ? `/editor/${projectId}` : "/editor") under the comment "bare /editor can't resolve a wizard draft". Step 2's import exit never got the same treatment — #428's fix covered only the projectId === null case.

Fix

One line in src/lib/wizard/completeWizard.ts, right after the if (!projectId) return; at :50:

// The draft is a finished project now, so bare /editor must resolve it (#727).
// The "don't pollute gf_project_id with an in-progress draft" rule
// (useWizardPersistence.ts:169) stops applying at exactly this point.
localStorage.setItem(PROJECT_ID_KEY, projectId);
localStorage.removeItem(storageKey());

completeWizard over patching StepUploadFloor.tsx:204: it is the single "the wizard is over, this project is real" seam and has four call sites, so this covers the import exit, the generate exit, the persistence subscriber's exit and a user who types /editor by hand — all at once. StepGenerate.tsx:109's existing guard becomes redundant but stays harmless. No stale pollution either: the next fresh /start deletes the key again at wizardSession.ts:17.

Also worth doing while in here

Both are one-liners on the same failure path, neither is the reported bug:

  • runImport can reject. src/lib/mappedin-import/runImport.ts:27-33 runs extractFloors, attachObjectCounts, extractLocations and source.buildings.map outside any try, while detectSource.ts documents "Never throws" and both callers await it bare. A throw there leaves isCheckingImport true forever in the wizard — and MappedinImportCard.tsx:56 disables all three ZIP/JSON/TXT pickers while checking, so only a reload recovers. Wrapping the body of runImport in a try that returns { ok: false, reason: "unreadable" } fixes both call sites without touching either component.
  • A Mappedin export zipped with its folder always reads as "unreadable". src/lib/mappedin/parse.ts:13-16 indexes files["manifest.geojson"] with flat keys and never strips a root prefix, so mall-demo-facility/manifest.geojson throws at :43. Verified: the #727 attachment re-zipped one folder deep returns { ok: false, reason: "unreadable" }. That is what right-click → Compress produces on both macOS and Windows, so it will be reported eventually.

Known and deliberately out of scope

The editor's Add Floor import dead-ends on failure: AddLevelModal.tsx:106 offers only Close and Retry Scan, and handleRetryScan (useAddLevel.ts:307) early-returns on !addedLevelId || !serverPath — both null after an import, so the button does nothing. Nothing ever sets phase back to "form". Separate screen, separate fix, filed when someone wants it.

Acceptance criteria

  • Reload the wizard mid-flow, import mall-demo-facility.zip at Step 2, press Continue to Editor → lands on /editor/<projectId> with the imported floor, not back on Create Project.
  • The same flow without a reload keeps working.
  • Leaving the wizard via Step 4 Generate still reaches the editor.
  • A fresh /start after finishing a project does not resume the old one.
  • runImport resolves { ok: false } instead of rejecting when an extractor throws — covered by a case in src/lib/mappedin-import/__tests__/runImport.test.ts.
  • A folder-prefixed Mappedin zip imports.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Fixed, plus one more the demo turned up. PR #731 → development.

The bounce

completeWizard now writes gf_project_id before dropping the blob (8191b22). Chosen over patching the exit because it is the single "the wizard is over, this project is real" seam — four call sites — so the import exit, the generate exit, the persistence subscriber and a hand-typed /editor are all covered at once.

Bare /editor does not resolve when pushed from here

Writing the key turned out to be necessary but not sufficient. Measured in a real Chrome window: router.push("/editor") from this exit renders a blank page for 30s+ and the redirect effect never runs — a reload clears it in about two seconds, and the same URL loaded fresh redirects normally. Headless masked it entirely, which is why it only surfaced while recording the demo.

Step 4's exits never had the problem because they go straight to /editor/<projectId>. This exit now does the same (3ca43a7), which removes the wait as well as the dependency on the redirect.

The two extras, as scoped

  • runImport runs its extractors inside the try that guards detection, so it returns the typed failure both callers already handle instead of stranding their spinners.
  • parseMappedinExport strips one shared root folder, so an export zipped by right-click → Compress imports.

Verification

Each fix has a test, and each was confirmed to fail without its fix. The first runImport test written here was vacuous — an arrayBuffer rejection is already caught upstream — so it was replaced with a mocked extractor throw that reaches the actually-unguarded region.

Against the attachment on #727:

flat:           ok floors=1 locs=34 buildings=1
folder-wrapped: ok floors=1 locs=34 buildings=1   <- was FAIL unreadable

pnpm test 160 files / 1391 passed · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

A 60 fps demo walks the whole path and asserts rather than narrates: it fails if the URL is not project-scoped, or if the folder-wrapped export shows the failure alert. Lives in .playwright-mcp/demo/729/ — not committed, that path is gitignored.

Left open

The editor's Add Floor import still dead-ends on failure (Retry Scan is a no-op after an import, and nothing returns phase to "form"). Out of scope here as filed.

The navigation change has no unit test — the branch mirrors StepGenerate.tsx:109 line for line, and reaching it in jsdom means driving a real file through the import modal. The demo covers it instead.

Commits: 8191b22, 3ca43a7

issues.display_title: Issue #732: fix(editor): Add Floor's Retry Scan does nothing when a Mappedin import fails
issues.main_description_html:
When a Mappedin import fails in the editor's Add Floor modal, the error screen offers Close and Retry Scan — and Retry Scan does nothing at all. No spinner, no error, no state change. The button is not disabled and gives no feedback, so the only way forward is to notice that nothing happened and press Close instead.

Found while fixing #729. Not part of that fix — different screen, and the wizard's own import card is fine (it shows a role="alert" with "Choose a file again to retry" and re-enables its pickers).

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

handleRetryScan is written for the AI-scan failure, not the import failure:

// src/components/editor/add-level/useAddLevel.ts:306-310
const handleRetryScan = () => {
  if (!addedLevelId || !serverPath) return;
  setScanError(null);
  scanAddedFloor(addedLevelId, serverPath, "retry_floor");
};

Both guards are null on the import path. An imported floor is never uploaded, so serverPath is never set (:95 only runs after /api/upload), and addedLevelId is only stamped by addFloorOnce (:228), which the import path never reaches. The import failure branch does exactly two things — setScanError(...) then setPhase("error") (:179-182) — and the phase === "error" screen renders Close plus Retry Scan unconditionally (src/components/editor/AddLevelModal.tsx:104-112).

The MapThru .txt import has the same shape: its catch at :164 also lands on phase: "error" without an upload, so Retry Scan is dead there too.

Nothing anywhere sets phase back to "form" — grep shows setPhase at :164, :169, :179, :184, :259, :292 and no "form" among them. The user is not permanently stuck, because EditorPanel.tsx:231 renders the modal as {showAddLevel && <AddLevelModal …/>}, so Close unmounts it and reopening starts clean. The defect is the silent no-op button, not a trap.

Fix

Make the error screen's action match the failure it is showing. phase === "error" is reached from two different places and only one of them has something to retry, so the button should follow that:

  • scan failure (addedLevelId and serverPath both set) — keep Retry Scan as it is
  • import failure (neither set) — offer Try Another File, which clears scanError and returns phase to "form", putting the user back on the picker without closing the modal

That is one conditional in AddLevelModal.tsx plus a setPhase("form") handler in useAddLevel.ts. Nothing else changes, and the scan path is untouched.

Acceptance criteria

  • An import failure in Add Floor (a non-Mappedin zip, or a .txt that is not a floorplan export) shows an action that returns to the picker, and pressing it does return there with the error cleared.
  • A scan failure still shows Retry Scan, and it still re-scans the floor it added.
  • No button on the error screen is ever a no-op.
  • Close still works from both failures, and reopening Add Floor starts on the form.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Fixed. PR #734 -> development, commit 1f16992.

The error screen now asks which failure it is showing. A failed scan uploaded an image and added the level it would re-target, so it keeps Retry Scan exactly as it was. A failed import has nothing to retry, so it gets Try Another File, which clears the error and returns phase to "form" — back on the picker without closing the modal. One conditional in AddLevelModal.tsx, one flag and one handler in useAddLevel.ts.

Correcting this issue's own description

The body above calls the old behaviour something the user could not recover from. That is wrong, and worth recording rather than quietly fixing: EditorPanel.tsx:231 renders the modal as {showAddLevel && <AddLevelModal …/>}, so Close unmounts it and reopening always started clean. The real defect was narrower — the button that looked like the way forward silently did nothing.

Verification

Three tests in src/components/editor/__tests__/AddLevelModal.importError.test.tsx, driving the real component with junk bytes through the import picker so runImport genuinely fails:

  1. a failed import offers Try Another File, and no Retry Scan
  2. pressing it clears the error and puts the picker back
  3. a failed scan still offers Retry Scan

Stashing the fix confirms 1 and 2 fail without it. 3 passes either way, which is the point — it guards behaviour that must not change.

pnpm test 161 files / 1390 passed · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

A 60 fps demo drives the same path in the editor and asserts rather than narrates: it fails if the error screen still reads "Retry Scan", and it fails if pressing the new button leaves the error on screen — which is what the old no-op would have done. Lives in .playwright-mcp/demo/732/, not committed (that path is gitignored). Nothing is added to the demo project: the import fails and the run ends on Cancel.

Cut from development, so it does not contain #729 (PR #731, still open). Different files, either order.

issues.display_title: Issue #736: fix(import): a Mappedin export without kinds/ imports with every object dropped
issues.main_description_html:
square-one-mall.zip imports "successfully" — 2 floors, 369 Information records and 15 categories all land, the review modal is green — but all 780 geometry features are silently discarded. Every floor row reads 0 objects, the editor panel reads All 0, the Map tab reads Total Objects 0, and canvasDataToGeoJson returns an empty FeatureCollection, so nothing draws. Reported as #728.

Measured on development:

parse     -> floors=2  locations=369  buildings=1
             Level 1 (f_5ae882cc…001) geometry = 318 features
             Level 2 (f_5ae8863…002) geometry = 462 features
convert   -> both levels: walls=0 areas=0 shapes=0 points=0 safety=0 doors=0
runImport -> ok, objectCount = 0 and 0

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Root cause

src/lib/mappedin/convert.ts:248:

const kind = floor.kinds[feature.properties.id];

Every classification branch below it compares kind to a string literal — :251 room/hallway, :264 wall, :278 object, :287 poi — and there is no else. This export ships no kinds/ directory, so parse.ts:124 (readJson<KindsMap>(files, \kinds/${id}.json`) ?? {}) hands convertFlooran empty map,kindisundefined` for all 780 features, and every one is dropped with no counter, no warning and no throw.

The import still reports success because the only emptiness gate is floors.length === 0 && locations.length === 0 (detectSource.ts:70, mirrored at runImport.ts:36). Two floors and 369 locations, so total geometry loss cannot trip it.

This is a second Mappedin export flavour, not a bad file

#727 mall-demo-facility.zip (imports fine) #728 square-one-mall.zip
classifier kinds/f_*.json → wall / room / object / poi cms/layers.json → layer names
geometry 165 LineString + 33 MultiLineString + 55 Polygon + 85 Point Polygon + Point only, zero LineStrings
extras walkable/, nonwalkable/, annotations/ cms/, floorImages/, textAreas/, outdoors.json

Every parser in src/lib/mappedin/ was written against the kinds flavour only. Nothing reads cms/, layers.json, floorImages/, textAreas/ or outdoors.json.

Everything in this export is a polygon at some scale: 9×13 m retail units (Polygon, 140 on L1), up to a 489×502 m site slab (Floor, 1).

Fix

One expression at convert.ts:248, plus a comment naming the simplification:

// This export flavour ships no kinds/ — every feature is a polygon classified by
// cms/layers.json layer name instead, so nothing matched and the whole floor was
// dropped (#728). A kind-less Polygon cannot occur in a kinds-flavour export
// (checked against every bundle in samples/ and #727), so no format sniffing is
// needed: treat it as a room, and keep a Point that a location is anchored to.
// ponytail: coarse on purpose — see "Deliberately not fixed" below.
const kind =
  floor.kinds[feature.properties.id] ??
  (feature.geometry.type === "Polygon"
    ? "room"
    : feature.geometry.type === "Point" && anchorMap.has(feature.properties.id)
      ? "poi"
      : undefined);

Measured with this applied: L1 0 → 278 areas, L2 0 → 432, and 443 of them carry a real tenant name from locations.json ("Simons", "Scotiabank", "Lucky Lotto Centre") through the existing anchor map; the rest fall back to Room N. canvasDataToGeoJson emits {area: 278} flat and {area: 278, ghost-area: 432} stacked, so it renders. All 81 existing tests under src/lib/mappedin and src/lib/mappedin-import still pass.

The Point half is not optional: 12 tenants are anchored only to Point geometry and stay invisible without it — Victoria's Secret PINK, Starbucks (At Indigo), Centre Court, Grand Rotunda, The Food District, Food Central, CIBC ATMs, Canada Post (Inside Shoppers Drug Mart), Raffi Jewellers, Motor Coach Drop-Off & Pick-Up Area, Outdoor, Clip. The 50 pure connection entrances stay dropped, which is correct — they are navigation anchors, not objects.

Nothing downstream needs walls: floorHasGeometry is walls.length > 0 || areas.length > 0, the map's area layers give fill, outline, label and 3D extrusion on their own, and levelBBox grows over areas. An area-only floor is a fully supported shape of a floor — the code just never produced one before.

Deliberately not fixed here

Each is real, measured, and worth its own task rather than being smuggled into a one-expression fix:

  • Doors stay 0. convert.ts:313 requires a connection's entrance to be a LineString; all 50 here (14 door, 11 escalator, 6 elevator, 1 stairs) are Points. A door has no segment to derive from a single point, and inventing one is the wrong-classification failure mode.
  • Coarse classification. 36 thin Wall ribbons, 23 Void openings and the site-wide Floor slab all import as rooms. The app has an exact open-to-below area type that Void should use.
  • 45 duplicate polygons on L2 (21 byte-identical outer-ring groups) import as stacked co-planar twins with duplicate labels and duplicate object rows. directContainment cannot cut equal-area twins.
  • 6 polygons have interior rings that are dropped — convert.ts:253 and :278 read coordinates[0] only. The L2 Wall donut is 96.8% hole.
  • First-paint cost. 710 areas make the first canvasDataToGeoJson take ~0.7–1.7 s (directContainment is O(n²)); it is WeakMap-cached, so later calls are ~70–90 ms.

A layer-name-driven mapping was designed and rejected for now: as drafted it would have deleted 23 named tenants (Exterior Building → skipped: Cineplex, LCBO, Spence Diamonds…) and hidden 35 more (Connections → hallway, which layer-definitions.ts:79 filters out of the label layer). If it is ever built, key it off default-style.json — it sits at the zip root, exists in both flavours, covers 710/710 polygons and carries real per-layer extrusion heights — not off cms/layers.json.

Acceptance criteria

  • Importing square-one-mall.zip shows non-zero objects per floor in the review modal (L1 278, L2 432).
  • The imported floors render on the Map tab — filled, outlined and labelled areas, not an empty canvas.
  • Anchored tenants keep their names and infoId links; the 12 Point-only tenants are among them.
  • The kinds-flavour exports are unchanged: #727 mall-demo and samples/ still import with the same counts as before (the sample-zip.int.test.ts regression net stays green).
  • A test covers a kind-less Polygon becoming an area and a kind-less anchored Point becoming a poi.
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit green.

RESULT

Fixed. PR #737 -> development. Commits 5fccd59, f135925.

A kind-less Polygon now reads as a room and a kind-less Point is kept when a location is anchored to it, at the one line every feature passes through. No format sniffing: a kind-less Polygon cannot occur in a kinds export, checked against every bundle in samples/ and #727.

#728 square-one   Level 1  0 -> 292 objects   (278 areas + 14 points)
                  Level 2  0 -> 437 objects   (432 areas +  5 points)
                  443 areas carry a real tenant name via the existing anchor map
#727 mall-demo    Level 1  297 -> 297   unchanged

A second fix the demo forced

With the import working, the floors arrive as areas and no walls — and the 3D pane covered them with "This level has no walls to preview in 3D. Switch to the Editor tab to draw walls." while the floor was drawn underneath it. Editor3DMapView.tsx:375 gated that placeholder on walls.length > 0, but areas extrude on their own through fp-area-extrusion-* and the view already wires hover handlers to those layers. The placeholder now asks for geometry; wall editing still asks for walls, which is right.

This also corrects something stated during the investigation: areas alone do render and extrude, but that panel-level gate short-circuited the whole preview before it mattered.

Verification

Three tests in src/lib/mappedin/__tests__/convert.test.ts — a kind-less Polygon becomes an area keeping its anchored name, a kind-less anchored Point becomes a poi while an unanchored one is dropped, and a kinds export is untouched. Stashing the fix confirms the first two fail without it; the third passes either way, which is the point.

pnpm test 161 files / 1397 passed · pnpm lint 0 errors · pnpm exec tsc --noEmit clean.

Demo at .playwright-mcp/demo/736/ (gitignored): reads the object count off the review modal and throws if either floor is 0, then ends on the floors rendered in the editor with their tenant names.

Still open, as scoped above

Doors stay 0 (Point entrances), classification stays coarse (Wall ribbons, Void, the site slab all read as rooms), 45 duplicate L2 polygons stack, 6 interior rings are dropped, first paint is ~0.7-1.7 s on 710 areas. All recorded in the body above; each wants the layer names, which is a bigger change than the report needs.

issues.display_title: Issue #730: Object safety annotations do not appear in preview and live project modes
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Safety annotations (Fire Exit, First Aid, Fire Extinguisher, Assembly Point, AED) are visible in the editor but do not appear in preview mode (/preview/[projectId], in-editor Preview overlay) or in the published/live viewer (/v/[key], /embed/[key]).

Repro

  1. Editor → place a safety annotation on a floor (do not link it to an Information record).
  2. Open Preview, or publish and open the live/embed link.
  3. The safety pin is missing from the map. It is still there when you go back to the editor.

Root cause

A safety annotation is created with no infoId — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interactions.ts:184 pushes { id, x, y, annotationType } only. So "unlinked" is the default state for every safety annotation.

Preview, live and embed all mount the same component (PreviewOverlay), and it drops unlinked objects in two places:

  1. Canvas pin (the actual safety glyph: colour + abbreviation) — src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx:254
    if (!informationRecords.some((r) => r.id === a.infoId)) continue;
    Introduced by cee63aa fix(preview): unlinked geometry is no longer publicly interactive (#461). Before that commit the pin drew unconditionally — this is the regression.
  2. DOM marker label — PreviewOverlay.tsx:714 passes showUnlinked={false}, and MapObjectMarkers.tsx:124 filters it.linked && !it.hidden. Predates #461, so after #461 nothing draws an unlinked safety pin publicly.

The editor has no such gate (Editor3DMapView.tsx:195, src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts:370), hence editor-only visibility.

Ruled out during investigation: persistence/publish payload (safety annotations round-trip fine), computeMarkerAnchors (already emits kind: "safety"), the showSafety toggle (preview hardcodes visibility.safety: true).

Scope of the fix

Safety pins are self-describing — the annotation type carries its own label, colour and glyph — so unlike areas and shapes they do not need an Information link to be meaningful in public modes. #461 stays intact for geometry.

  • Remove the link gate at PreviewOverlay.tsx:254 so unlinked safety pins draw in preview/live/embed.
  • Extract the marker loop into src/lib/preview/safetyMarkers.ts (mirrors the existing src/lib/preview/panoMarkers.ts pattern) so it has a unit-test home.
  • Do not flip showUnlinked to true — MapObjectMarkers.tsx:382 renders unlinked markers with a red unlink badge, which is an editor-only affordance and must not leak into public modes.

Clicking an unlinked pin already behaves: PreviewOverlay.tsx:675 resolves heading: safetyTypeLabel(...) and PreviewInfoCard.tsx:49 falls back to the heading, so the card shows e.g. "Fire Extinguisher / Safety" instead of the empty card #461 removed.

Acceptance criteria

  • An unlinked safety annotation renders in preview, /v/[key] and /embed/[key], with the correct type colour and abbreviation.
  • A linked safety annotation keeps its current behaviour (pin + name label).
  • The selected safety annotation still draws no duplicate pin under its selection label.
  • Unlinked areas / shapes / points stay non-interactive and unlabelled in public modes (#461 and #278 unchanged).
  • No red unlink badge appears in preview/live/embed.
  • pnpm test passes, including a new test for the unlinked case.

Out of scope (follow-ups)

  • Preview search cannot find unlinked safety annotations — PreviewOverlay.tsx:616-627 collect() returns [] without an Information record. Fixing it means making SearchTarget.info optional, which ripples into AreaAutocomplete / SearchAreaPanel.
  • src/lib/collab/sync.ts:105 mergeAreaMetadata backfills accessPoints and buildingId from the previous level but not safetyAnnotations, so a snapshot missing that key can wipe them and the autosave persists the loss. Affects the editor too — separate issue.
